calls.reason: TheAgentCompany reports only 30% completion, and OpenAI acknowledges agent errors. These show reliability limits, but do not establish that a major commonsense advance is necessary to overcome them.

PolyMATH documents spatial errors, while Sparkle shows improvements transferring to new tasks. Neither tracks corrected failures and subsequent variants, leaving the explanation for recurring errors unclear.
Disney and NASA document useful simulation applications, while Wang et al. show successful physical reasoning. These selected examples do not establish the claimed broad difference in effectiveness.

SpaRC and PhyGenBench document language-model and video weaknesses. PHYRE and the successful fluid-simulation study leave the contemporary breadth of simulation-based reasoning unclear; the claim covers all three approaches.

TheAgentCompany's 30% completion and Remote Labor Index's 2.5% automation show substantial shortfalls. They do not establish whether commonsense competence is necessary for eventual reliable deployment.

OpenAI describes Sora generating latent patches decoded into pixels and acknowledges frequent unrealistic physics at launch. Its reported implicit object persistence does not amount to an explicit object-based scene representation.
